body:
This is "fixed" in the new sandbox implementation, however the new sandbox uses symlinks for all input files, which generally work fine, but may cause other issues.

If this is still a problem for you, please let me know and re-open this bug.

This still seems to be a problem in Bazel 0.3.2.  See associated bugs I filed against Python below.

http://bugs.python.org/issue28424
http://bugs.python.org/issue28425

To expand on this, if `__init__.py` is a symlink to a regular file, it's fine, but if it's a symlink to /dev/null, it doesn't work correctly.  So the fix would be to create a regular empty file and link to that.  I guess there must be some reason we don't make all the `__init__.py` files regular empty files.

The relevant code seems to be this:

https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/sandbox/SpawnHelpers.java#L167

I can generate a minimal testcase but I don't see that Bazel currently has any Python tests in the repo, so I'm not sure where to put it.  Basically

```
=== BUILD ===
py_binary(
    name="a",
    srcs=["a.py","mypackage/b.py"],
    srcs_version="PY3")
```

```
=== a.py ===
import mypackage.b
assert hasattr(mypackage, "__file__")
```

```
=== b.py doesn't matter ===
```

```
$ git clone -b dgreiman/bazel-issue-1458 https://github.com/google/subpar.git

$ /opt/bin/bazel version
..........
Build label: 0.3.2
Build target: bazel-out/local-fastbuild/bin/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/BazelServer_deploy.jar
Build time: Fri Oct 7 17:25:10 2016 (1475861110)
Build timestamp: 1475861110
Build timestamp as int: 1475861110

$ /opt/bin/bazel test //...
//:a_PY2                                                                 PASSED in 0.1s
//:a_PY3                                                                 FAILED in 0.1s
```

Yes.  Just tested in Bazel 0.4.2, and the sandbox still creates symlinks to /dev/null

The Python folks have decided not to fix this in Python, for compatibility reasons: /dev/null is not a regular file, so there would have to be some tricky special casing, and some portability concerns for all the various OS's that handle this slightly differently, all to support a fairly unusual use case.

The Python docs are going to be clarified that `__init__.py` must be a regular file, i.e. symlinking to /dev/null is not supported.

```
$ /opt/bin/bazel test --test_output=streamed //...
WARNING: Streamed test output requested so all tests will be run locally, without sharding, one at a time.
INFO: Found 2 test targets...
total 12
lrwxrwxrwx 1 nobody nogroup   9 Dec  8 18:35 __init__.py -> /dev/null
```

I also tested normal module (i.e. not \_\_init\_\_) source files, and Python 3 doesn't handle those either.  So you shouldn't link anything that supposed to be a Python source file to /dev/null, you should just create a regular 0 length file.

Totally agree. Symlinking to /dev/null is the wrong thing to do here, creating an empty file instead is the right thing.

The culprit is here: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/fa3f55a8785c28253b2f836ddc84e994e48edd7f/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/sandbox/SpawnHelpers.java#L142

I'll definitely fix this, but not sure if I can get it done before my vacation in January, as I only have ~3 working days left before the holidays start here.
A fix for this is now (finally) in code review. Sorry that it took so long.

issue.title: First cut at a foo_image rule

repository.name: rules_docker
repository.description: Rules for building and handling Docker images with Bazel

issue.body:
This change is a first-cut at attempting a `foo_image` rule that directly assembles a Docker image compatible with `foo_binary`, but leveraging a sharded archive format (vs. a mono-archive format like [PAR](https://github.com/google/subpar) or "deploy JAR")

The advantage of the sharded archive format is simple:  **We want to translate build-time incrementality into redeployment incrementality.**

By enabling the partitioning of dependencies into their own layers, in a binary agnostic fashion, we enable:
1. sharing of those dependencies across different images that depend on them
1. no republishing of those dependencies' layers when they haven't changed
1. no repulling unchanged dependencies' layers

In this model, what gets repushed/repulled can be made a direct function of Bazel's library-level incrementality.
